no catalogue class disables a laser system output and diode emission together; cap.optics.shutter.v1 models an optical shutter, not the laser's electrical output and diode state, and cap.device.configure.v1 would only write a field
no catalogue class sends a single external trigger pulse; the clone's command is DRV:CYC:TRIG 1 followed by DRV:CYC:TRIG 0 and no class models a pulse

cap.measure.current.v1 reads current only and cap.optics.set_power.v1 sets optical power in mW, while the clone exposes the diode drive current in mA and reads its maximum from the connected laser, so no class binds this setting

cap.thermal.setpoint.v1 binds thermal.zone, instrument.incubator and lab.thermal_block, not optics.laser, and cap.measure.temperature.v1 reads temperature only; the clone exposes the TEC target as a component setting of the laser, so no class binds it

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check; the gate raised no warning and no finding, and the evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. Model-authored and unreviewed: reviewed_by stays null, nothing ran on hardware, and the hardware factory was never imported. Risk is R2, above the card's R1 floor: MHS/spec/04-safety.md section 2.1 classes a laser above class 1 as R2, and the clone states no IEC laser class, so the package neither claims class 1 nor claims R3 without a class 3B or 4 statement; SAFE-045 is met by the turn_off action declared safe_state=True, not by a cited hardware e-stop. NOT COVERED: calibration (Laser.calibrate), tune and sweep mode, manual-mode heater channels, photodiode readouts, trigger inversion and trigger mode; the driver exposes the system output, the diode state and current, the TEC readings and target, and a single trigger pulse. The diode-current and TEC-target actions call the upstream component objects (laser.diode, laser.tec); the gate's Recorder wraps only the top-level Laser, so those calls appear in its log as the diode and tec attribute reads, and both inputs are operator_required, so G6 exercises them only through its synthetic overlay and G8 through site-limits.example.json. The example overlay's 0 to 100 mA and 15 to 35 Cel are examples for the installed unit, not device facts; an operator replaces them with the rated ranges. The card's helper hint PythonObjectDriver was not used: the interface is a vendor SDK object with nested component objects and per-component limits, which the direct Driver expresses; the card's decision direct-driver is unchanged. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording, and the clone contains no upstream simulator. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
